correctness.rationale: For every n>=1, fix the two spine labels and count the n independent pages. When a spine label is empty, its missing-colour condition is imposed by inclusion-exclusion. The five exhaustive spine-label types yield precisely A0^n - 4(1+x)A1^n + 6x^(2n) + 4x B1^n + 6x^2 B2^n + 4x^3 B3^n + x^4(1+x)^(4n). An independent literal-label enumeration confirmed all coefficients for n=1..4, with minimum pairs (2,4),(3,4),(4,5),(4,1). For n>=4, other contributions have degree >=5 and x^4 (1+x)^(4n) gives unique degree-4 term. The finite enumerations corroborate but do not establish all n; the spine-case proof does.

originality.rationale: The existing rainbow/prism bijection transforms the claim into the ordinary domination polynomial of K_{1,n} square C_4. The full published complete-multipartite two-rainbow enumerator does not cover B_n for n>=2: nonadjacent vertices a1 and a2 on different pages have different neighborhoods {s,b1} and {s,b2}, unlike any nonadjacent pair in a complete multipartite graph. Inspected foundational sources give minima/definitions, not every coefficient on this graph family; no checked broader theorem directly implies the all-n expression. An older unindexed prism-domination enumerator remains possible.
residual_risks: The foundational 2007 prism equivalence paper was available through abstract/bibliographic material rather than a complete readable primary text.
An earlier domination polynomial of K_{1,n} Cartesian C4, or equivalent square-book all-weight tabulation, could be unindexed; absence in current searches is not a priority certificate.

value.rationale: Counting all rainbow dominating functions of square book graphs by weight is a natural finer enumerative invariant than their minimum domination number. The common-spine interaction yields a seven-term exact all-order polynomial and sharp low-weight transition at four pages. Researchers can use the full polynomial or equivalent K1,n square C4 domination polynomial independently of any global classification.
